name: Taking of the Cocopah country without a treaty of purchase (Royce Area 686)
aka: Royce 686, Cocopa: country claimed by them at beginning of their relations with the U.S.
citation: No treaty or statute: Royce records that no treaty of purchase was ever made and that the United States assumed title to their country
promises: Not a treaty. Royce records that no treaty of purchase was ever made with the Cocopa and that the United States assumed title to their country, shown on his Arizona map No. 1.
Royce notes that most of them had been concentrated on the Colorado River reservation.
compensation: No claims award for Cocopah aboriginal land was found.
today: Royce himself records that the United States assumed title without any treaty of purchase, but no court, claims-commission, Act of Congress or government finding about this taking was found. A full-text search of the Indian Claims Commission decisions for 'Cocopa' and 'Cocopah' returned only passing mentions in the Mohave and Quechan findings, and the Court of Claims volumes list no Cocopah case.

sources.title: Charles C. Royce, Indian Land Cessions in the United States (18th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, 1899), schedule p. 922-923, area 686

openQuestions: Whether the Cocopah filed a claim with the Indian Claims Commission was not settled; none appears in the Oklahoma State University collection. The Commission's 1978 Final Report docket list was not checked. A web search pointed only to a 1970 district court suit by the Native American Rights Fund over accretion land at the reservation, which was not opened.
The 1886-10-01 date in treaties.json is a Royce heading, not a date of any taking; Royce 686 is undated. Not edited.
treaties.json presentDayTribes was empty; treaty-corrections.json now lists the Cocopah Tribe of Arizona.
The Cocopah Indian Tribe's history page (cocopah.com/history) returned 404; the nation voice is missing.

Audit 2026-11-08: Royce pp. 922-923 re-read (area 686: "No treaty of purchase was ever made with this tribe. The U. S. assumed title to their country"). ICC full text "Cocopah" and "Cocopa" returns only the Mohave (186) and Quechan (323) findings; the Court of Claims index has no Cocopa or Cocopah case. No-breach-found stands.
